claim: Doyle and Rossetti prove (Theorem 1) that the full Laplace spectrum of a compact hyperbolic 2-orbifold determines, and is determined by, the volume, the total mirror-boundary length, the number of conepoints of each order (counting a mirror corner as half a conepoint), and the number of closed geodesics of each length and orientability class.
stance_target: The manuscript's Section 1.3(a) attribution of qualitative cone-order determinacy solely to Ucar
scope_conditions: Compact hyperbolic 2-orbifold, not necessarily connected or orientable; proved specifically for constant curvature -1 (the manuscript's own setting), 6 years before Ucar's 2017 thesis
quoted_support: The Laplace spectrum of M determines, and is determined by, the following data: 1. the volume; 2. the total length of the mirror boundary; 3. the number of conepoints of each order, counting a mirror corner as half a conepoint of the corresponding order; 4. the number of closed geodesics of each length and orientability class.

claim: The Doyle-Rossetti determinacy result is proved via the Selberg trace formula applied to the entire Laplace spectrum (recovering the character of a representation of Isom(H^2) on the frame bundle), not via any finite subset or finite number of heat-trace coefficients.
stance_target: Whether cone-order determinacy for hyperbolic 2-orbifolds is a full-spectrum or finite-coefficient result
quoted_support: The character determines the Laplace spectrum of M, and indeed, the spectrum of any other natural operator. Theorem 1 tells us that for hyperbolic 2-orbifolds, we can go back the other way, and recover the character from the Laplace spectrum.

claim: Doyle and Rossetti themselves flag that, as of 2011/2014, it is an OPEN and unproven question whether the full cone-order/singular-set data of a hyperbolic 2-orbifold can be recovered from a finite number of heat-trace coefficients; they note the DGGW heat-trace approach 'restricted to hyperbolic 2-orbifolds... don't yield complete information about the singular set' and that recovery 'presumably... could be extracted... by looking at higher and higher terms in the asymptotic expansion' -- language suggesting an unbounded/unproven number of terms, not an established finite threshold.
stance_target: The manuscript's priority claim (Section 1.3(b)) to give the first exact finite-coefficient determinacy threshold for hyperbolic cone orbifolds
scope_conditions: Hyperbolic 2-orbifolds; heat-trace short-time-asymptotics approach specifically, as opposed to the Selberg-trace-formula approach used in this paper
quoted_support: Their results yield information about orbifolds of variable curvature, and in any dimension. Restricted to hyperbolic 2-orbifolds, the results they state don't yield complete information about the singular set. All this information is there in the short-time asymptotics of the heat trace, however, and presumably it could be extracted using their approach, by looking at higher and higher terms in the asymptotic expansion.

claim: Dryden and Strohmaier (arXiv:math/0504571, 'Huber's theorem for hyperbolic orbisurfaces') proved the same determinacy result as Doyle-Rossetti's Theorem 1, but restricted to ORIENTABLE hyperbolic 2-orbifolds, using wave-trace methods rather than the Selberg trace formula.
stance_target: Prior art for cone-order determinacy in hyperbolic 2-orbifolds
quoted_support: By looking at the wave trace, Dryden and Strohmaier [8] proved the result of Theorem 1 for orientable hyperbolic 2-orbifolds. While they did not consider non-orientable surfaces or orbifolds...

claim: arXiv:1103.4372 (Doyle-Rossetti) has never been published in a peer-reviewed journal; the only citable identifier is the arXiv-issued DataCite DOI 10.48550/arXiv.1103.4372. Confirmed independently via the arXiv abstract page (no 'Journal reference' field present) and via the Semantic Scholar API (venue field empty, journal listed only as 'arXiv: Differential Geometry').
stance_target: Publication record / correct DOI for Doyle-Rossetti in the manuscript's bibliography

claim: Doyle-Rossetti's proof technique (Selberg trace formula, requiring homogeneous constant-curvature geometry) is explicitly contrasted by the authors with wave and heat approaches, which 'can work in great generality' but for which 'the Selberg method will beat the wave and heat approaches' on constant-curvature spaces specifically.
stance_target: Methodological comparison of full-spectrum vs. heat-trace approaches for orbifold determinacy
quoted_support: The beauty of the wave and heat approaches is that they can work in great generality. The Selberg method depends on having spaces whose underlying geometry is homogeneous, such as manifolds and orbifolds of constant curvature. For studying such spaces, it is a good bet that the Selberg method will beat the wave and heat approaches.
